# TagZ Foods: Valuation and Profitability Analysis

TagZ Foods, a premium Indian snack brand known for its popped chips, faces significant challenges in valuation, scalability, and repeat consumption despite rapid sales growth and Shark Tank exposure. The company reported a revenue of ₹23 crore in FY23 but incurred net losses between ₹4.6 to ₹10.7 crore, leading to a valuation drop after its acquisition by Reliance at ₹28 crore. The case study highlights the need for improved margins, effective branding, and a stronger consumer fit to ensure long-term viability.

results.title: TagZ Foods Reports 41% Revenue Growth in FY25 | Startup Pedia posted on the topic | LinkedIn
results.content:
In May 2023, the company raised $2 million in a Pre-Series A round led by 9Unicorns (now 100Unicorns), with participation from Dexter Angels, Agility Ventures, and actor Rannvijay Singha. Prior to this, TagZ had raised $1.2 million in seed funding in 2020 from a group of angel investors. The company also appeared on the first season of Shark Tank India, securing investment from Namita Thapar and Ashneer Grover.
In a significant development, Reliance Consumer Products, a subsidiary of Reliance Retail, reportedly acquired TagZ Foods in November 2024 for approximately Rs 28 crore ($3.5 million). The deal has been described as a distress sale, following the brand’s challenges in scaling operations and managing sustained losses.
#startuppedia #startupbusiness #startupnews [...] The D2C Gen Z snacks brand TagZ reported revenue of Rs 26.6 crore in FY25, marking a 41% increase from Rs 18.8 crore in FY24, according to its financial statements sourced from the Registrar of Companies (RoC).
The company’s operating revenue, however, declined sharply by 90% to Rs 1.3 crore in FY25, down from Rs 14.14 crore in FY24. Meanwhile, other income surged 5.3X to Rs 25.3 crore in FY25 from Rs 4.7 crore in FY24. This spike was primarily driven by gains from the sale of intangible assets during the year, which contributed Rs 23.5 crore. [...] On the expense front, total expenditure declined by 18% to Rs 19 crore in FY25 from Rs 23.12 crore in FY24. Direct expenses, including manufacturing, freight, labour, and packaging, fell sharply by 87% to Rs 1 crore in FY25, compared to Rs 7.8 crore in FY24. The cost of goods sold stood at Rs 60 lakh in FY25, down significantly from Rs 6.5 crore in FY24.
Employee benefit expenses also declined by 63% to Rs 1.1 crore in FY25 from Rs 3 crore in FY24. In contrast, advertising and sales promotion expenses increased to Rs 4 crore in FY25, up from Rs 1.5 crore in FY24.
The company reported a net profit of Rs 7.5 crore in FY25, compared to a net loss of Rs 4.3 crore in FY24.
